claims.claim: Sequence-length-free norm generalization is a new property of the Born head.
claims.finding: Known transformer result bounds input, value/readout and score matrices. It is not automatic coverage of the nonlinear learned Born score/value class, and absence of an explicit T term alone supplies no novel comparison or Macro explanation.

claims.claim: Writing the Born weights as softmax proves the bilinear theorem applies unchanged.
claims.finding: On valid tokens alpha=softmax(log(q+EPS)); log-score oscillation<=log((1+EPS)/EPS). But the original score is bilinear in token/CLS features with bounded matrices; log Born overlap from shared circuit/effects is nonlinear. Complete score covers, input/value/readout radii and multiclass loss bridge still need proof. No numerical or full-model equivalence asserted.

claims.claim: Low-dimensional NW oracle rate follows from3qubits.
claims.finding: Source n counts iid observed covariate/outcome pairs; current summation is contextual within-text tokens and learned signed utilities. Source assumes true regression psi(X)=phi(TX), Gaussian PSD bandwidth family, boundedobservations/predictions and Kfold squared-risk selection. Threequbits do not prove a low-index true task function, whole-head bottleneck or currentCE/Macro oracle rate. General theorem has gamma term; practical local CV is not automatically gamma0.

claims.claim: Exactv1 displayed bandwidth substitution independently certifies the stated rate.
claims.finding: Conditional only on displayed log(n)/h bias term and h_n(m)=V(nlogn)^(1/(m+2)), the ratio to displayed targetrate grows as(nlogn)^(1/(m+2)). This says that displayed upper-bound substitution is insufficient; it does not show true risk violates the rate, refute the original theorem, inspect the missing supplement or certify a squared-bandwidth repair.

claims.claim: These applicability failures demote the actual ordinaryL4.
claims.finding: Generic sequence-free and low-index transfer routes close as direct L5 contributions only. Old trained-head utility/localalignment evidence unchanged; no no-benefit or universal generalization-impossibility claim.
